ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Hepatology Referral — Evel Knievel — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: New patient: chronic pain from old fractures, diabetes, and raised liver tests with low platelets on today's tests: hepatitis C and liver work-up, NSAIDs stopped, alcohol counseling, and hepatology review booked

text.paragraph: Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and platelets of 118 on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a 57-year-old retired stunt performer who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1962, drinks most evenings and has type 2 diabetes. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV and an abdominal ultrasound are ordered. Please see him within three weeks to confirm the cause, stage his liver disease and plan treatment. [S]
Urgency: Within three weeks; sooner if he develops jaundice, ascites, bleeding or confusion. [S]

list.item: Does he have chronic hepatitis C, and what is the stage of his liver disease?
Which antiviral treatment do you recommend, and are there interactions with his medicines?
Does he need endoscopy or treatment for portal hypertension?
What surveillance does he need for liver cancer and other complications, and does he need a transplant evaluation?
How should his pain, diabetes and alcohol use be managed safely with his liver disease?

text.paragraph: Dozens of fractures from stunt crashes, including a broken pelvis, with many blood transfusions in the 1960s and 1970s. Three or four drinks most evenings for years (AUDIT-C 7); never smoked; no drug use. Type 2 diabetes on metformin, A1c 7.4%. Chronic back, hip and knee pain treated for years with ibuprofen 800 mg three times a day and omeprazole; both stopped today, with acetaminophen up to 2 g a day and diclofenac gel. Two falls in the past year without injury. Examination today: blood pressure 138/84, pulse 80; spider angiomas and palmar erythema; no jaundice, ascites or asterixis. Results today: hemoglobin 13.9 g/dL, platelets 118, creatinine 0.92 mg/dL, eGFR 97, ALT 88, AST 96, alkaline phosphatase 104 U/L, bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL, albumin 3.6 g/dL, INR 1.1, glucose 162 mg/dL, LDL 112 mg/dL. FIB-4 4.94. No known allergies. He wants to keep walking and does not want strong pain pills [S]

list.item: Pain in the back, hips and knees every day from old fractures, worse in the morning and after travel; ibuprofen three times a day for years. [S]
Tired for months; noticed small red spots on his chest and wonders whether the old transfusions or his drinking have hurt his liver. [S]
He wants to keep walking and playing golf and does not want to depend on strong pain pills. [S]
Two falls in the past year; he worries about breaking another bone. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Robert Craig Knievel was born on October 17, 1938, in the copper-mining town of Butte, Montana, and was raised by his grandparents. [D]

He began his daredevil career in 1965 with a touring motorcycle show. His crash after jumping the fountains at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, dated 1968 in the wire obituaries, put him in the hospital, by their account in a coma for a month. [D]

In 1974 his rocket-powered cycle failed in an attempt to jump Idaho's Snake River Canyon. In 1975 the crash landing of his jump over 13 buses at Wembley Stadium in London broke his pelvis. In the winter of 1976 an attempt to jump a tank of live sharks in Chicago left him with a concussion and two broken arms, after which he retired from major jumps. [D]

Guinness World Records lists him as holding the record for the most broken bones in a lifetime, with 433 bone fractures by the end of 1975. His obituaries instead said he suffered nearly 40 broken bones before he retired in 1980. [D]

list.item: Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and low platelets (118) on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a man of 57 who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1962 and drinks most evenings: chronic liver disease, most likely hepatitis C, must be excluded. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV, liver ultrasound and hepatology review ordered: active, confirmed [S]
Type 2 diabetes on metformin, A1c 7.4%: active, confirmed [S]

Chronic pain in the back, hips, pelvis and knees after dozens of fractures from stunt crashes, including a broken pelvis; ibuprofen stopped, and managed without oral NSAIDs or opioids: active, confirmed [S]

Liver work-up for raised transaminases and low platelets: hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody, hepatitis A IgG, HIV, INR, ultrasound of the abdomen, and FIB-4 from today's tests. Guideline: AASLD-IDSA HCV Guidance: Recommendations for Testing, Managing, and Treating Hepatitis C. Simplified HCV treatment algorithm for treatment-naive adults with compensated cirrhosis (2023); Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening (2020) [S]

Pain care safe in liver disease: stop ibuprofen and omeprazole; acetaminophen up to 2 g a day; topical diclofenac for the knees; no opioids; physical and aquatic therapy; heat, pacing and sleep routines; pain coping skills. Guideline: Rakoski M, Goyal P, Spencer-Safier M, et al. Pain management in patients with cirrhosis. Clin Liver Dis (Hoboken) 2018;11(6):135-140 (PMID 30992804) (2018); Dowell D, et al. CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain - United States, 2022. MMWR Recomm Rep 2022;71(3):1-95 (PMID 36327391) (2022) [S]

Alcohol: brief counseling toward stopping completely, because alcohol speeds liver scarring; follow-up AUDIT-C at each visit; counseling or medicine for alcohol use offered if he cannot stop. Guideline: Crabb DW, et al. Diagnosis and Treatment of Alcohol-Associated Liver Diseases: 2019 Practice Guidance From the AASLD. Hepatology 2020;71(1):306-333 (PMID 31314133) (2019); Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018) [S]

Falls and fractures: physical therapy and a home safety review; vitamin D; bone density scan, since cirrhosis, alcohol and many old fractures raise the risk of osteoporosis. Guideline: Watts NB, et al. Osteoporosis in men: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(6):1802-1822 (PMID 22675062) (2012); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, osteoporosis and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Depression and distress screening at each visit, and plain explanations with written information. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, osteoporosis and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Referral to hepatology, Mei-Ling Okonkwo, MD, ordered 1996-01-12 [S]
